newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb kills two, Algerian forces kill 9 rebels-paper.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills two, Algerian forces kill 9 rebels-paper.

text.p: A bomb killed two girls south of Algiers as bereaved villagers in a nearby hamlet buried some 50 relatives slaughtered by Moslem rebels, an Algerian newspaper said on Wednesday.
The home-made bomb exploded by a house near Chrea, about 50 km (about 30 miles) south of Algiers, killing the two girls aged 10 and 12 years on Tuesday, said El Watan newspaper.
The same day, survivors of a massacre in neighbouring Si Zerrouk hamlet buried some 50 relatives killed by about 100 rebels on Sunday, the newspaper said.
The assailants broke into the villagers' homes and cut the throats of the residents, including women and babies, newspapers said.
About 60,000 people have been killed since early 1992 when authorities cancelled a general election in which the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding lead.

Earlier this month, FIS chief Abassi Madani was freed half way through a 12-year term for threatening state security. He vowed shortly after his release that he and his supporters would strive to stop the bloodshed.
More than 170 civilians have been slaughtered by rebels in the past week in Blida province and neighbouring Tipaza region.
Newspapers said the latest massacres were rebel retaliation for a military offensive on guerrilla strongholds in the past three weeks in which up to 300 rebels were killed and scores captured.

According to the newspapers, the rebels belonged to cells of the Armed Islamic Group (GIA) who had gathered to plot strategy when they were trapped. Algerian officials blame the GIA for most of the massacres of civilians in isolated villages.

L'Authentique newspaper on Wednesday said security forces killed eight rebels, including a cell leader named Abu Meriem, in a Monday-Tuesday operation in Ksar el Boukhari, 90 km (55 miles) southeast of Algiers.
In Algiers, government forces killed one rebel and arrested three on Tuesday in a clash near the German embassy, said Al Alam Assiassi newspaper.
On Tuesday, the FIS armed wing, the Islamic Salvation Army (AIS), vowed to pursue the conflict against Algerian authorities.
In a statement, it denied reports that large numbers of rebels were surrendering, saying the reports were part of a media campaign to "mutilate the image of jihad (holy struggle) in Algeria".
It was not possible to authenticate the statement, faxed to an international news agency in Paris.
Both the AIS and the FIS have distanced themselves from the indiscriminate killing of civilians.
The AIS statement made no reference to the security force operation earlier this month, nor did it mention the massacres.
